 By Flint McColgan | flint.mccolgan@bostonherald.com PUBLISHED: October 31, 2026 at 8:41 PM EDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... A man pleaded guilty in federal court in Boston to stealing the identity of a U.S. citizen from Puerto Rico in order to fraudulently obtain more than $20,000 in federally funded welfare benefits.
 An undated photo of Erpawi Roque Collado included in an affidavit supporting his fraud charge. Courtesy/US District Court 
 Erpawi Roque Collado, 54, is a lawful permanent resident of the United States — not a citizen — who was born in the Dominican Republic and moved here as a child. Federal authorities arrested him and charged him by criminal complaint in March with illegal acquisition or use of supplemental nutritional assistance program benefits.
 He pleaded guilty to Friday to two charges: unlawfully obtaining Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits and theft of government money. The former can land him in federal prison for 20 years and the latter for 10 years.
 Incident Summary
 BPD responded to 279 incidents in the 24-hour period ending at 10 a.m. Saturday, according to the department’s incident log. Those included two robberies, three aggravated assaults, two residential burglaries, four thefts from vehicles, one stolen vehicle, and 14 instances of miscellaneous larceny.
 Arrests
 All of the below-named defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty.
 — Marcus Hoplins, 63 Waldeck St., Dorchester. External warrant.
 — Shawn-Matthew Smith, 345 Harrison Ave., Boston. External warrant.
 — Lamekia Mervin, 200 Cove Way, Quincy. Assault and battery with a dangerous weapon.
 — Erik Swanson, 346 South Road, Bedford. Breaking and entering a boat or vehicle in the nighttime for felony.
 — Martin Suuna, 25 River St., Winchester. Assault and battery with a dangerous weapon.
